stem: Which of the following made long-distance trade more possible for the Aztecs than for the Incas?
options: (B) The use of sea trade routes
explanation: [SOURCE MATERIAL - REWRITE REQUIRED] The Aztecs lived in a more temperate climate than the Incas and did not have the same mountainous obstacles preventing the transport of goods. Both the Incas and the Aztecs had road systems (A); both carried on little sea trade (B); both produced marketable goods (C).

stem: Which of the American peoples was closest to the Persians in their administrative style?
explanation:
[SOURCE MATERIAL - REWRITE REQUIRED] Like the Persians, the Incas were adept at integrating subject peoples into their empire as long as their subjects refrained from rebellion. Both the Incas and the Persians also constructed roads to serve as communication links to the various parts of their empires. The Aztecs were noted for their exceptionally harsh treatment of conquered peoples (C). The Mayas (A) did not demonstrate the imperial organizational skills of the Incas, while the Mississippians did not establish an empire (B).

 The most extensive Incan public works were highway systems, which facilitated travel and trade.
